'''Bharti Enterprises Limited''' is an Indian [[multinational corporation|multinational]] [[Conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]], headquartered in [[Delhi]]. It was founded in 1976 by [[Sunil Bharti Mittal]]. Bharti Enterprises owns businesses spanning across [[telecommunication]]s, [[manufacturing]], [[insurance]], [[real estate]], [[hospitality]]. The group's flagship company, [[Bharti Airtel]], is a telecom service provider with operations in more than 18 countries across Asia, Africa and Europe. The company ranks amongst the top two [[List of mobile network operators|mobile network operators globally]] by number of subscribers.

==History==
The company was founded by [[Sunil Bharti Mittal]] with his two siblings in 1976. The company initially started manufacturing bicycles before diversifying into other sectors. It entered into telecommunications industry in 1995.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Bharti Airtel Ltd. - Money Control |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/company-facts/bhartiairtel/history/BA08 |work=Money Control}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Kumar |first=Shivendra |date=2023-11-22 |title=Bharti Airtel begins IPO process of subsidiary Bharti Hexacom: Report |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/ipos/fpos/bharti-airtel-begins-ipo-process-of-subsidiary-bharti-hexacom-report/articleshow/105414762.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2024-03-22 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

==Companies==
[[File:Bharti-Airtel-Country-Map.PNG|thumb|right|300px|Coverage map of Bharti Airtel across 18 countries]]
Bharti is present in many sectors with the largest revenue contribution coming from the telecom industry.

===Bharti Airtel===
{{Main|Bharti Airtel}}
Bharti Telecom (BTL), is a [[holding company]] of Bharti Airtel with Bharti Enterprises and [[SingTel]] owning 50.56 percent and 49.44 percent, respectively, in BTL, which in turn owns 35.80 percent of Bharti Airtel.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Das |first1=Saikat |last2=Parbat |first2=Kalyan |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/companies/airtel-promoter-arm-to-raise-rs-1380-cr-to-participate-in-the-rights-issue/articleshow/87113123.cms |title=Airtel promoter arm to raise Rs 1,380 cr, to participate in the rights issue |work=The Economic Times |date=2021-10-19 |accessdate=2021-11-15 }}</ref>

Bharti Airtel is the third largest mobile operator in the world, in subscriber base, and has a presence across 18 countries.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/topic/Airtel|title=Airtel: Latest News, Videos and Photos {{!}} Times of India|date=2017-09-22|website=The Times of India|access-date=2017-09-26}}</ref> The company is India's second largest integrated telecom company in customer base and offers mobile, fixed line, high speed home broadband, M-commerce, DTH and enterprise service.

=== Indus Towers ===
{{main|Indus Towers}}
Indus Towers Limited is an telecommunications infrastructure company offering passive [[Infrastructure as a service|infrastructure services]] to mobile network operators and other wireless services providers. Headquartered in [[Gurugram]], [[Haryana]], Indus Towers was incorporated in November 2007 by [[Bharti Infratel]] (a subsidiary of Bharti Airtel), [[Vodafone India|Vodafone Essar]], and [[Idea Cellular]], to provide shared telecom infrastructure to telecom operators on a non-discriminatory basis.<ref>{{Cite news |title=TERI and Indus Towers jointly ink MoU on developing innovative renewable energy solutions |language=en-US |work=The Financial Express |url=http://www.financialexpress.com/archive/teri-and-indus-towers-jointly-ink-mou-on-developing-innovative-renewable-energy-solutions/318567/ |access-date=2017-07-25}}</ref>

Bharti Infratel merged with Indus Towers on 19 November 2020, creating one of the largest [[Cell site|mobile tower]] infrastructure operators in the world.<ref>{{cite news |date=20 November 2020 |title=Largest tower company in world outside China! Indus Towers, Bharti Infratel merger complete |publisher=[[Business Today (India)|Business Today]] |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/sectors/telecom/largest-tower-company-indus-towers-bharti-infratel-merger-complete/story/422492.html}}</ref> Post-merger, Bharti Airtel holds a 36.73% stake in Indus Towers, with [[Vodafone|Vodafone Group]] holding 28.12%,<ref name=":03">{{cite web |date=19 November 2020 |title=Bharti Infratel, Indus Towers merger done; VIL sells Indus stake for ₹3,760 cr |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/bharti-infratel-indus-towers-merger-complete-vodafone-idea-sells-indus-stake-for-rs-3-760-cr-11605806024934.html |access-date=21 May 2023 |website=mint |language=en}}</ref> and 3.1% shares held by [[Providence Equity]].<ref name="shareholding">{{Cite web |date=2020-11-19 |title=Bharti Infratel, Indus Towers complete merger process |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/info-tech/bharti-infratel-indus-towers-complete-merger-process/article33135455.ece |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=www.thehindubusinessline.com |language=en}}</ref> Indus Towers has over 192,874 towers and 342,831 co-locations and a nationwide presence covering all 22 telecom circles.<ref name="livemint.com">{{cite news |last1=Guha |first1=Ishita |date=28 January 2021 |title=Indus Towers Q3 net profit up 2% at ₹1,360 crore |publisher=[[Livemint]] |url=https://www.industowers.com/investor/company-profile/}}</ref>

In June 2024, Vodafone sold its entire stake in the company to Bharti Airtel, thus the company become a direct subsidiary of Bharti Airtel.<ref>{{cite news|date=19 June 2024 |title=Vodafone sells 18.0% stake in Indus Towers|publisher=Vodafone|url=https://www.vodafone.com/news/corporate-and-financial/indus-share-sale}}</ref>

===Beetel Teletech===
Beetel Teletech Limited, formerly Brightstar Telecommunications India Limited, was founded in 1985. The company manufactures and distributes mobile accessories, IT peripherals, network and enterprise solutions, and landline phones. Its manufacturing unit is located in [[Ludhiana]], [[Punjab, India|Punjab]]. It is also a major distributor of IT and telecom products from international brands such as [[Avaya]], [[Poly Inc.|Poly]], [[Samsung]], [[Panasonic]], [[Huawei]], [[QSC Audio Products|QSC]], [[Radwin]], [[Ruckus Networks|Ruckus]], [[RAD Data Communications|RAD]] and Actelis.<ref>{{cite web |title=Introduction |url=https://www.beetel.in/introduction/ |access-date=21 May 2023 |website=Beetel}}</ref>

Beetel Teletech launched a 7-inch [[Android (operating system)|Android]] tablet priced at {{INRConvert|9.999|k|year=2011}} in India on 18 August 2011. The offering was intended to capitalise on the expected demand for cheap computing devices in the world's fastest-growing and second-largest mobile phone market.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bharti Unit Launches Android Tablet in India|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424053111903596904576515333409395922|access-date=18 August 2011|newspaper=The Wall Street Journal|date=17 August 2011|first=Kenan|last=Machado|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160117185009/http://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424053111903596904576515333409395922|archive-date=17 January 2016|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Gourmet Investments ===
Gourmet Investments Pvt Ltd was founded in 2012 by Ramit Mittal, the eldest son of Bharti Enterprises' vice chairman and managing director Rakesh Mittal, with support from the Bharti family office.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The man behind Ministry of Crab |url=https://www.dailyo.in/lifestyle/bharti-mittal-ramit-mittal-restaurants-food-industry-gourmet-food-crabs-fine-dining-22373 |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=www.dailyo.in |language=en}}</ref> The company signed a 50:50 joint venture partnership agreement with British restaurant chain [[PizzaExpress]] in 2012, and opened the first outlet in [[Mumbai]] later that year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=UK's PizzaExpress to debut in India soon; hires CEO |url=https://www.rediff.com/business/slide-show/slide-show-1-uks-pizzaexpress-to-debut-in-india-soon-hires-ceo/20120702.htm |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=Rediff |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-04-26 |title=UK legacy brand PizzaExpress now in Bengaluru |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/life-and-style/food/uk-legacy-brand-pizzaexpress-now-in-bengaluru/article66777337.ece |access-date=2023-05-21 |issn=0971-751X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Sinha |first=Sanjeev |date=2015-03-23 |title=We want PizzaExpress to become the benchmark for pizzas in India: Sanjay Nandrajog |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/opinion/interviews/we-want-pizzaexpress-to-become-the-benchmark-for-pizzas-in-india-sanjay-nandrajog/articleshow/46659859.cms |access-date=2023-05-21 |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

in 2018, Gourmet Investments partnered with Sri Lankan restaurant chain Ministry of Crab, owned by cricketers [[Kumar Sangakkara|Kumara Sangakara]], [[Mahela Jayawardene]] and chef [[Dharshan Munidasa]], to launch outlets in India.<ref>{{Cite web |last=www.ETRetail.com |title=Gourmet Investments to bring Sri Lankan seafood joint to India - ET Retail |url=https://retail.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/food-entertainment/food-services/gourmet-investments-to-bring-sri-lankan-seafood-joint-to-india/62381755 |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=ETRetail.com |language=en}}</ref> The first outlet was opened at [[Khar, Mumbai|Khar]], Mumbai in February 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mumbai Welcomes Ministry of Crab |url=http://bwhotelier.businessworld.in/article/Mumbai-Welcomes-Ministry-of-Crab/18-02-2019-167269 |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=BW Hotelier |language=en}}</ref> In 2019, the company acquired some Indian outlets of the American restaurant chain [[Chili's]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2019-03-11 |title=Bharti co GIPL in talks to buy Chili’s |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/bharti-co-gipl-in-talks-to-buy-chilis/articleshow/68350714.cms |access-date=2023-05-21 |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> Gourmet Investments operates 16 outlets of PizzaExpress, Chili's and Ministry of Crab as of February 2023.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Haidar |first=Faizan |last2=Bhushan |first2=Ratna |date=2023-02-07 |title=Bharti Family Office firm to bring US-based food chain PF Chang's to India |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/cons-products/food/bharti-family-office-firm-to-bring-us-based-food-chain-pf-changs-to-india/articleshow/97668217.cms |access-date=2023-05-21 |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> In February 2023, Gourmet Investments reportedly signed an agreement with American restaurant chain [[P. === Bharti AXA Life Insurance ===
Bharti AXA Life Insurance Company Limited is a joint venture between Bharti Enterprises and French insurance company [[Axa|AXA]] established in 2006. Bharti Enterprises holds a 51% stake in the joint venture, with AXA holding the remaining 49%.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bharti AXA Life Insurance posts maiden profit of Rs 5 cr in FY18 |url=https://www.dnaindia.com/business/report-bharti-axa-life-insurance-posts-maiden-profit-of-rs-5-cr-in-fy18-2622466 |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=DNA India |language=en}}</ref> The company has a nationwide presence through 251 branches across India.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jermoe |first=Karthik |date=2023-02-28 |title=Bharti AXA-Unity Bank in bancassurance tie-up to tap 1.5 mn customers |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/finance/bharti-axa-life-insurance-unity-bank-establish-bancassurance-partnership-123022800790_1.html |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=www.business-standard.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

Bharti Enterprises sought to exit its insurance services business beginning negotiations with [[Reliance Industries]] to sell its stake in both Bharti AXA Life Insurance and Bharti AXA General Insurance in 2016. However, no agreement was reached.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2020-08-11 |title=Insurer ICICI Lombard in talks to buy Bharti AXA |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/business-news/insurer-icici-lombard-in-talks-to-buy-bharti-axa/story-s7TaYwvfayq00XfGJktbZP.html |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref> A consortium of the [[Hinduja Group]] and the [[Abu Dhabi Investment Authority]] reportedly entered negotiations to acquire Bharti AXA Life Insurance in December 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2021-12-03 |title=Hinduja and ADIA combine in talks to but AXA stake in life insurance JV with Bharti |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/insure/hinduja-and-adia-combine-in-talks-to-but-axa-stake-in-life-insurance-jv-with-bharti/articleshow/88054247.cms |access-date=2023-05-21 |issn=0013-0389}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-12-01 |title=Hinduja-ADIA consortium in talks to buy AXA stake In life insurance JV with Bharti |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/hinduja-adia-consortium-in-talks-to-buy-axa-stake-in-life-insurance-jv-with-bharti-7782431.html |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=Moneycontrol |language=en}}</ref>

=== Bharti Space & OneWeb ===
{{main|OneWeb}}

A 50% stake in [[OneWeb]] was acquired in July 2020, being a joint venture with the [[Government of the United Kingdom|UK Government]] for [[Broadband#Computer networks|broadband]] [[Satellite Internet access|satellite Internet services]].<ref>{{cite news |date=3 July 2020 |title=UK government takes £400m stake in satellite firm OneWeb |publisher=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-53279783}}</ref>

=== Norlake Hospitality ===
Norlake Hospitality Limited is a real estate and hospitality property developer in Europe and the United States, in partnership with London-based hospitality company Ennismore.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bharti Website: Our Companies |url=https://www.bharti.com/our-company-international.html |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=www.bharti.com}}</ref> Headquartered in London, it was founded on 18 May 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NORLAKE HOSPITALITY LIMITED overview - Find and update company information - GOV.UK |url=https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/08075340 |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk |language=en}}</ref>

=== Emtel ===
Bharti Enterprises acquired a 25% stake in [[Emtel]] which is a Mauritius-based telecommunications company, on 27 April 2015 through its subsidiary, Indian Continent Investment Limited (ICIL).<ref>{{cite web |title=Brief Rationale Emtel Limited ("Emtel") |url=http://www.careratingsafrica.com/downloads/Emtel%20Limited-%20Brief%20Rationale%2012-June%202020.pdf |website=Care Ratings Africa |access-date=21 May 2023 |page=2 |archive-date=21 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230521221844/http://www.careratingsafrica.com/downloads/Emtel%20Limited-%20Brief%20Rationale%2012-June%202020.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== BT Group ===
Bharti announced that it would acquire a 24.5% stake in British telecommunications company [[BT Group]] on 12 August 2024.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Aulakh |first=Gulveen |date=2024-08-12 |title=Bharti Enterprises to pick up 24.5% stake in UK’s British Telecom Group {{!}} Company Business News |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/bharti-enterprises-bt-group-sunil-bharti-mittal-india-uk-trade-telecom-investment-bharti-televentures-altice-uk-11723448499321.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250121150746/https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/bharti-enterprises-bt-group-sunil-bharti-mittal-india-uk-trade-telecom-investment-bharti-televentures-altice-uk-11723448499321.html |archive-date=21 January 2025 |access-date=2025-07-15 |work=mint |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref> The acquisition was completed on 16 December 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=UK govt approves Bharti Global's acquisition of 24.5% stake in BT |url=https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/uk-govt-approves-bharti-global-s-acquisition-of-24-5-stake-in-bt-124121701191_1.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250101051127/https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/uk-govt-approves-bharti-global-s-acquisition-of-24-5-stake-in-bt-124121701191_1.html |archive-date=1 January 2025 |access-date=2025-07-15 |website=www.business-standard.com |language=en-US |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Philanthropy==
[[File:Bharti School of Management.jpg|thumb|Bharti School of Management in [[IIT Delhi]] campus.]]
Bharti Foundation is the philanthropic arm of Bharti Enterprises. The Foundation has established schools in villages across India and offers free quality education with free books, uniform and mid day meals to poor children.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://online.barrons.com/article/SB125935466529866955.html |title= The 25 Best Givers |author= Suzanne McGee |date= 30 November 2009 |work= Barron's|access-date=1 April 2010}}</ref>
Satya Bharti School Program' – the Foundation's flagship program is running 254 schools in six States serving over 45,000 rural children, free of cost. The other educational initiatives including the – Satya Bharti School, Quality Support and Learning Centre Programs, are currently reaching out to over 350,000 underprivileged children in 16 states. Other Program of the Foundation making considerable impact among the underprivileged sections is – 'Satya Bharti Abhiyan' (Sanitation).

In 2017, the Bharti Family pledged 10% of wealth (approx. Rs 70 billion) towards Philanthropy to set up Satya Bharti University, a world-class University to offer education to deserving youth from economically weaker sections of society.{{citation needed|date=July 2020}}

==Former companies==
=== Hike ===
{{main|Hike Messenger}}
Hike Private Limited was founded by [[Kavin Bharti Mittal]] in 2012. The company launched Hike Messenger, a [[freeware]], [[cross-platform]] [[instant messaging]] (IM), [[Voice over IP]] (VoIP) application, on 12 December 2012.<ref name="hikeblog">{{cite web |date=December 12, 2012 |title=Hike Launches Globally |url=http://hike.in/blog/launch/12-12-12-hike-goes-global-win-an-iphone-5/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402081817/http://hike.in/blog/launch/12-12-12-hike-goes-global-win-an-iphone-5/ |archive-date=April 2, 2015 |access-date=August 12, 2014 |publisher=Bharti SoftBank}}</ref> Hike Messenger had more than 100 million registered users as of August 2016. It was rebranded as Hike Sticker Chat in April 2019. The app was shut down in January 2021. The company stated that it would pivot to building a new bite-sized gaming service named Rush.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2021-01-19 |title=Hike shuts messaging app, shifts focus to new social offerings |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/technology/hike-shuts-down-hike-sticker-chat-to-pivot-to-other-social-products/articleshow/80328203.cms |access-date=2023-05-21 |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>
===Centum Learning===
Centum Learning Limited, formerly Bharti Learning Systems Limited, was a wholly owned subsidiary of Bharti Enterprises established in 2007.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-09-15 |title=Upgrad acquires corporate training platform Centum Learning |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/startups/upgrad-acquires-centum-learning/articleshow/94221161.cms |access-date=2023-05-21 |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> Centum Learning was acquired by education technology firm upGrad in a [[Stock swap|share swap]] deal in September 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-09-15 |title=upGrad acquires corporate training solutions provider Centum Learning |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/startup/upgrad-acquires-corporate-training-solutions-provider-centum-learning-14731801.htm |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=cnbctv18.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== Del Monte Foods ===
Bharti Enterprises and investment group E.L. Rothschild established a 50:50 joint venture called FieldFresh Foods in 2004 to produce and export fresh vegetables and fruits. In 2007, Singapore-based Del Monte Pacific Limited (a subsidiary of [[Del Monte Foods]]) acquired a 40.1% stake from Rothschild for $20.8 million.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=Bhushan |first=Ratna |date=2024-03-01 |title=Bharti Enterprises loses appetite for Del Monte JV, to focus on telecom |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/cons-products/food/bharti-enterprises-loses-appetite-for-del-monte-jv-to-focus-on-telecom/articleshow/108082879.cms |access-date=2025-07-15 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> The company also sold processed food and beverage products in India and South Asia under the Del Monte brand.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bharti Website: Our Companies |url=https://www.bharti.com/our-company-india.html |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=www.bharti.com}}</ref> The company was renamed Del Monte Foods Private Limited in 2021.<ref name=":2" /> Del Monte Foods was acquired by Agro Tech Foods Ltd in a share swap deal on 6 February 2025, with Bharti Enterprises receiving a 21% stake and Del Monte Pacific getting a 14% stake in Agro Tech Foods.<ref>{{Cite web |last=www.ETHospitalityWorld.com |title=Agro Tech Foods completes acquisition of Del Monte Foods from Bharti Enterprises - ET HospitalityWorld |url=https://hospitality.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/operations/food-and-beverages/agro-tech-foods-completes-acquisition-of-del-monte-foods-from-bharti-enterprises/118019868 |access-date=2025-07-15 |website=ETHospitalityWorld.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Bharti AXA General Insurance===
Bharti AXA General Insurance Company Limited was a joint venture between Bharti Enterprises and French insurance company [[Axa|AXA]] incorporated on 13 July 2007.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bharti AXA General Insurance Company Limited Information |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/company/ |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=The Economic Times |language=en |archive-date=8 May 2019 |archive-url=http://webarchive.loc.gov/all/20190508200151/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/company/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Bharti Enterprises held a 51% stake in the joint venture, with AXA holding the remaining 49%. The company had a nationwide presence through 135 branches across India.<ref>{{cite web |title=About us |url=https://www.bharti-axagi.co.in/about-us |website=bharti-axagi.co.in |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210325032324/https://www.bharti-axagi.co.in/about-us |archive-date=25 March 2021 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Bharti Enterprises sought to exit its insurance services business beginning negotiations with [[Reliance Industries]] to sell its stake in both Bharti AXA General Insurance and Bharti AXA Life Insurance in 2016. However, no agreement was reached.<ref name=":0" />

On 21 August 2020, Bharti AXA General Insurance and [[ICICI Lombard]] signed a definitive agreement for the latter to acquire the former in an all stock deal. Per the terms of the agreement, shareholders of Bharti AXA General Insurance received 2 shares of ICICI Lombard for every 115 shares they held.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2020-08-22 |title=ICICI Lombard signs definitive agreement to acquire non-life insurance business of Bharti AXA |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/icici-lombard-signs-definitive-agreement-to-acquire-non-life-insurance-business-of-bharti-axa/article32419262.ece |access-date=2023-05-21 |issn=0971-751X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Laskar |first=Anirudh |date=2020-08-22 |title=ICICI Lombard, Bharti AXA to merge general insurance businesses |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/icici-lombard-bharti-axa-to-merge-general-insurance-businesses-11598068493984.html |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=mint |language=en}}</ref> The acquisition was completed on 8 September 2020.<ref name="ReferenceA">{{Cite web |date=2021-09-09 |title=ICICI Lombard ceases to be ICICI Bank subsidiary post Bharti AXA merger |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/icici-lombard-ceases-to-be-icici-bank-subsidiary-post-bharti-axa-merger-11631199555368.html |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=mint |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Bharti AXA General Insurance Merger with ICICI Lombard |url=https://www.icicilombard.com/info-center/bharti-axagi-merger-announcement-customer-faqs}}</ref> Bharti Enterprises received 18.23 million shares in ICICI Lombard and AXA received 17.52 million shares,<ref name="ReferenceA"/> worth a combined total of EUR 664 million.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ICICI Lombard, Bharti AXA merger completed |url=https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/asia/news/breaking-news/icici-lombard-bharti-axa-merger-completed-309572.aspx |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=www.insurancebusinessmag.com |language=en}}</ref> The [[Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority|Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India]] granted in-principle approval to the acquisition in November 2020,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-11-27 |title=Irdai approves acquisition of Bharti AXA General Insurance by ICICI Lombard === Bharti Infratel ===
{{main|Bharti Infratel}}

Bharti Infratel Limited was a telecommunications infrastructure company that provided telecom infrastructure such as telecom towers, fiber networks and other related infrastructure.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=Investor Relations - Bharti Infratel |url=https://www.bharti-infratel.com/cps-portal/web/company-profile.html |access-date=24 June 2020 |website=www.bharti-infratel.com}}</ref> Headquartered in [[Gurugram]], [[Haryana]], the company was established by Bharti Airtel in July 2007 by [[Corporate spin-off|spinning-off]] its [[Cell site|mobile towers]] to a new wholly owned subsidiary. Bharti Infratel was the first Indian company to start a tower infrastructure sharing business. It was India's largest consolidated tower infrastructure company, directly owning 95,372 towers as on 31 March 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=Company Profile |url=http://www.bharti-infratel.com/cps-portal/web/company-profile.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200706103906/http://www.bharti-infratel.com/cps-portal/web/company-profile.html#1 |archive-date=6 July 2020 |website=Bharti Infratel}}</ref>

Bharti Infratel was merged with Indus Towers on 19 November 2020. Prior to the merger, Bharti Infratel held a 42% stake in Indus Towers. Bharti Airtel now holds a 36.73% stake in Indus Towers.<ref name=":03"/>

===Bharti Wal-Mart===
Bharti Wal-Mart Private Limited was a 50:50 joint venture between Bharti Retail (a subsidiary of Bharti Enterprises) and [[Walmart]] that operated a chain of [[Cash and carry (wholesale)|wholesale cash-and-carry]] retail stores in India. The two companies announced that they had signed an agreement to establish the company on 5 August 2007.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bharti Enterprises and Wal-Mart Join Hands in Wholesale Cash-and-Carry to Serve Small Retailers, Manufacturers and Farmers |url=https://corporate.walmart.com/newsroom/2007/08/05/bharti-enterprises-and-wal-mart-join-hands-in-wholesale-cash-and-carry-to-serve-small-retailers-manufacturers-and-farmers |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=Corporate - US |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2007-01-20 |title=Wal-Mart to enter India in Bharti retail venture |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-bharti-walmart-idUSDEL23218120061127 |access-date=2023-05-21}}</ref> In February 2009, Bharti Wal-Mart announced that the stores would be branded Best Price Modern Wholesale and that the first store would open in Punjab.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2009-02-03 |title=New name for Bharti JV with Wal-Mart |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/new-name-for-bharti-jv-with-wal-mart/articleshow/4067297.cms |access-date=2023-05-21 |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> The first Best Price Modern Wholesale opened in [[Amritsar]] in May 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bhandari |first=Bhupesh |last2=Rai |first2=Amit Ranjan |date=2009-11-10 |title=Inside Bharti Walmart |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/management/inside-bharti-walmart-109111000014_1.html |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=www.business-standard.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Bharti and Walmart ended the partnership in October 2013, with Walmart acquiring Bharti's stake in the joint venture. At the time the partnership was called off, Bharti Wal-Mart operated 19 Best Price Modern Wholesale stores.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tandon |first=Suneera |date=2013-10-09 |title=Wal-Mart, Bharti end India venture, look to move on |url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/ZhVnG46uEx5HBJEG9I1ISP/Bharti-WalMart-go-separate-ways.html |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=mint |language=en}}</ref>

=== Bharti Retail/Easyday ===
Bharti Retail Limited was established as a wholly owned subsidiary of Bharti Enterprises at the time it began its joint venture with Walmart. Bharti Retail operated a chain of convenience stores, supermarkets and hypermarkets under the brand name Easyday. The stores were wholly owned by Bharti Retail, while Bharti Wal-Mart provided the back-end, wholesaling and logistical support for the Easyday stores.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Mallet |first=Victor |last2=Kazmin |first2=Amy |date=2015-05-04 |title=Bharti Retail and Future Group to merge |work=Financial Times |url=https://www.ft.com/content/984d0c34-f25b-11e4-892a-00144feab7de |access-date=2023-05-21}}</ref>

In May 2015, [[Future Group]] acquired Bharti Retail in a deal worth around {{INRConvert|500|c|year=2015}}.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2015-05-05 |title=Kishore Biyani's Future group acquires Bharti Retail in an all-stock deal valued at Rs 500 crore |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/services/retail/kishore-biyanis-future-group-acquires-bharti-retail-in-an-all-stock-deal-valued-at-rs-500-crore/articleshow/47148446.cms |access-date=2023-05-21 |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> Following the acquisition, Bharti Enterprises received 9% stakes in Future Retail Limited (manages retail operations) and Future Enterprises Limited (manages infrastructure, investments and assets).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-05-04 |title=Future Group's retail business to merge with Bharti Retail |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/content/475575/future-groups-retail-business-merge.html |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref> At the time of the acquisition, Bharti Retail operated 216 Easyday stores.<ref name=":1" />

extract: Bharti Enterprises Limited is an Indian multinational conglomerate, headquartered in Delhi. It was founded in 1976 by Sunil Bharti Mittal. Bharti Enterprises owns businesses spanning across telecommunications, manufacturing, insurance, real estate, hospitality. The group's flagship company, Bharti Airtel, is a telecom service provider with operations in more than 18 countries across Asia, Africa and Europe. The company ranks amongst the top two mobile network operators globally by number of subscribers.
